title_en: The Fall Solo Six-Pack: Sports Games, the Return of Discretionary Macro, & AI Coming for Your Job
title_zh: Jon Caplis 秋季单人六连聊：体育、主观宏观回归、湖人税局与 AI 就业冲击
subtitle_zh: RCM 的 Jon Caplis 一人分饰主客，盘点青少年体育、主观宏观、湖人出售与 AI 就业六大话题
summary_zh: 本期 The Derivative（RCM Alternatives 出品）是主持人 Jon Caplis 的单人“六连聊”（solo six-pack），他一人分饰主持与嘉宾，为十月开篇盘点六个话题。其一，青少年体育：他坦言明知孩子打不进职业，却仍陪儿子奔波于各地旅行队（travel teams）赛事，因为孩子的比赛是有限供给；本周儿子在高尔夫分区赛（sectionals）以一杆之差无缘州赛，令他感慨。其二，CTA Expo 观感：主观宏观（discretionary macro）正成为当红策略，系统化与机器学习已成“入场门槛”（table stakes），人脑反成稀缺的原创交易来源。其三，湖人队出售：卖方 Mark Walter 用保险浮存金（insurance float）收购资产，买方（Iger 与 Kushner 兄弟）借税法在 15 年内摊销球员合同，估算每年约 8 亿美元抵税，实为买下“税收减免”。其四，犹他州顶级度假村之旅：从 Promontory 与 Pivotal 创始人在 2009 年以 3000 万美元抄底的往事，谈到 billionaire 的“迷你城市”，衍生出球童、水管工等“防 AI”体力岗位。其五，对照 Citrini 的 AI 论点与 ADP、Stanford 数据：入门级知识工作首当其冲（22 至 25 岁就业年内降 4.3%、连续 33 个月收缩），但向更广劳动力扩散尚未出现。其六为听众信箱，并预告下周迎来第二位真人嘉宾。本集以亲历与数据交织，展现一位另类投资人对体育、税局、财富分层与 AI 就业的独立判断。
description: The Fall Solo Six-Pack: Sports Games, the Return of Discretionary Macro, & AI Coming for Your Job

turns.en: Welcome to the Derivative by RCM Alternatives, send it. Hello there. Welcome back. You've found the Derivative brought to you by RCM Alternatives where we, part of the sponsors the CTA Expo here in town this week. I've been at a bunch of kids golf events, regionals and sectionals more on that in a quick second.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 RCM Alternatives 出品的 The Derivative，开录。大家好，欢迎回来。你正在收听的是 RCM Alternatives 带来的 The Derivative，这周我们是本地 CTA Expo（管理期货大会）的赞助方之一。我这几天一直在忙一堆青少年高尔夫比赛，地区赛（regionals）和分区赛（sectionals），这个待会儿细说。

turns.en: So we didn't have a guest last week and mess it up this week. So you get me on a solo six pack here to start October. Hard to believe it's fall already. So where do we start? Wanted to start out with youth sports, six pack number one, open that beer. I was told by a kidless friend, is that how I said that?
turns.zh: 上周我们没请嘉宾，这周索性也搞砸到底，所以就由我一个人来一期 solo six-pack（单人六连聊）给十月开个头。真不敢相信已经入秋了。那从哪儿聊起呢？我想先聊聊青少年体育，这是六连聊的第一罐，开啤。有位没孩子的朋友跟我说——我是这么说的吧？

turns.en: A friend without kids the other day. I turned down an invite to something to head to a kid softball game. And he said, basically, you know, you don't have to put them in all these travel teams. Your kids probably not going to go pro. That's only a good prank to tell you. And the kid will end up all right if you don't go to every game.
turns.zh: 前几天那位没孩子的朋友。我推掉了一个邀约，去看一场孩子的垒球赛。他基本上就是说，你知道，你没必要把孩子塞进所有这些旅行队（travel teams）。你家孩子多半打不了职业，那不过是忽悠你的好听说法。就算你不每场都到，孩子最后也不会差。

turns.en: So a few things done pack here. One, I know my kids aren't going pro. And I agree. The prevalence of travel teams and lessons and training has gotten a little bit at a hand. We talked about that on a pod with Scott Carl earlier this year, put that in the show notes. It is ridiculous.
turns.zh: 关于这罐聊几点。第一，我知道我家孩子打不了职业。而且我同意，旅行队、私教课和训练现在泛滥得有点失控（out of hand）。今年早些时候我们在一期节目里跟 Scott Carl 聊过这个，链接放在节目备注里了。真的很离谱。

turns.en: You have the teams called going pro pro prospect, future stars elite and such. It's like they're selling the berry flavored vape pens to preteens. Worst part is a lot of parents believe in this scam. I've talked to some who say that's their college savings plan, scary. But that was me. It's not our family. But we still do it. So why?
turns.zh: 那些队名都叫什么 'go pro prospect'、'future stars elite'（未来之星精英）之类的。就像在给十来岁的孩子卖莓味电子烟。最糟的是，很多家长真信这套骗局。我跟一些家长聊过，他们说这就是他们的大学教育金计划，吓人。但那不是我，我们家不是这样。可我们照样在做。那为什么呢？

turns.en: It's nuance. The high school picks people up the travel teams. The kid wants to start wants to play. That's extra lessons, extra works. So is it evil? Yes. Is it also maybe necessary to play sports in high school? Big Chicago school also yes. But to the other half of the friends comment.
turns.zh: 这事儿很微妙。高中校队是从旅行队里挑人的。孩子想首发、想上场，那就得加课、加练。所以它是坏事吗？是。那它是不是想在高中打上体育比赛可能又绕不开的一环？在芝加哥这种大城市，也是。不过再回到那位朋友话里的另一半。

turns.en: You don't have to go to every one of your kids games. I like going to the games. I love going to the games. I'm a sports fan in general. You've heard me talk bears and cubs on here. And this is the ultimate sport to be a fan in, right? You get to be court side on the field walking inside the ropes, whatever we want to call it.
turns.zh: 你不必每场孩子的比赛都到。我喜欢去看比赛，我热爱去看比赛。我本来就是个体育迷，你们听我在这节目里聊过 Bears（熊队）和 Cubs（小熊队）。而青少年比赛是当球迷的终极体验，对吧？你能坐在场边、站在球场里、走在围栏绳以内，随便你怎么叫它。

turns.en: You get to hear what the coach is telling the player. Get to see the player recover. Get to see the training. Get to see the mental side. But there's another bigger piece that this is finite, right? It's econ 101. There's only so much supply of your kids games. And then it's done.
turns.zh: 你能听到教练在跟球员说什么，能看到球员怎么调整恢复，能看到训练，能看到心理层面的东西。但还有一个更大的点是：这是有限的，对吧？这是经济学 101（入门常识）。孩子的比赛就那么点供给量，然后就没了。

turns.en: You can't make your kid 12 again and scalp some little league tickets and go watch them. Imagine if the bears were ceasing to exist as a team in two years. Maybe that's a bad example because they are looking at moving to Indiana. But imagine if ignoring that, imagine if they were never going to be any more bears games.
turns.zh: 你没法让孩子回到 12 岁，再去倒几张少棒联赛（little league）的票来看他们打。想象一下，如果 Bears 这支球队两年后就不复存在了——也许这个例子举得不好，因为他们确实在考虑搬去 Indiana（印第安纳州）。但先忽略这个，想象一下以后再也不会有 Bears 的比赛了。

turns.en: The tickets would be astronomical, right? You'd drop everything and anything to go get to as many of those games as possible before they were gone, which is what's happening in your kid's sports, right? There's only so many of them left, which brings me to the sad start to this week. My son's a senior on the golf team.
turns.zh: 那票价得是天价，对吧？你会放下一切，尽可能多赶几场去看，趁它们还没消失。而这正是你孩子体育比赛的情况，对吧？就只剩那么几场了。这就说到本周这个有点伤感的开头：我儿子是高尔夫校队的高四（senior）队员。

turns.en: He made it through regionals, played in sectionals. He was one under through nine and in second place. Everyone was cheering. Top 10, make it through. Then a double bogey, then a couple of pars, then a three put bogey, then another. And before I could get my heart rate back under 130, it was over. He missed going to state by stroke.
turns.zh: 他打进了地区赛，又打了分区赛。前九洞他低于标准杆一杆（one under），排在第二，大家都在欢呼，前十名就能晋级。然后一个双柏忌（double bogey），接着几个帕（par），然后一个三推柏忌，再来一个。还没等我把心率降回 130 以下，比赛就结束了。他以一杆之差（by a stroke）错过了州赛。

turns.en: So why do I go? Because I'm a fan of my kid, I'm a fan of sports. And there's only so many games left. And sadly, this week, no more games left for my senior. So if you're listening to this body, love you, proud of you. It was fun watching you over the years. All right, that was a sad start. Let's get a little cheerier here.
turns.zh: 那我为什么还去看？因为我是我孩子的粉丝，我是体育的粉丝，而且比赛就剩那么几场了。遗憾的是，这周我家这位高四球员再没有比赛可打了。所以如果你在听这期节目：爱你，为你骄傲，这些年看你打球很开心。好了，这是个伤感的开头，咱们来点开心的。

turns.en: But thought that needed to be said. It's a weird thing for people to be like, why do you go to your kid's sports?
turns.zh: 但我觉得这话得说。别人会问'你为什么去看孩子的比赛'，这本身就挺奇怪的。

turns.en: All right, number two, open it up. Was that the CTA expo yesterday? It was a conference that was around dozens and years ago, maybe eight dozen years ago. Took a few years off. Now has come back. But it's fun to see a lot of the same characters, people I've known for 20 years or more. I did a panel.
turns.zh: 好，第二罐，开。昨天那个是 CTA Expo。这是个多年前办过的会，可能好几十年前，中间停办了几年，现在又回来了。能见到很多老面孔、我认识 20 年甚至更久的人，很有意思。我参加了一个圆桌（panel）。

turns.en: We titled it by Builder Partner, RCM Sponsored Event. Basically, everyone said it's dumb to build in today's world. There's so many ways to outsource everything and anything, compliance to sales, to trade execution. I agree. That's why RCM is here. That's what we do for so many clients.
turns.zh: 圆桌标题是'自建还是合作'（build or partner），是 RCM 赞助的场次。基本上大家都说，在今天这个世界自己从头搭建（build）是很蠢的，有太多方式可以把一切外包出去——合规、销售、交易执行都行。我同意。这也正是 RCM 存在的意义，我们为这么多客户做的就是这件事。

turns.en: But anyway, I typically don't like to prep for a panel. And actually I sent an email to the fellow panelists last week, said there's a few things I hate more in life than panel prep calls, parentheses, green bay packers, slow drivers in the left lane, people who take their socks off on the plane.
turns.zh: 总之，我一般不喜欢为圆桌开准备会。其实上周我给同台嘉宾发了封邮件，说这辈子比圆桌准备会（panel prep call）更让我讨厌的事没几件——括号：Green Bay Packers（绿湾包装工队）、占着左道慢开的司机、在飞机上脱袜子的人。

turns.en: So beg them that we didn't need to do a call, and I think the panels go better that way. It's not that you're not prepared. You can prepare on your own. You can tell them kind of some of the things you want to talk about. But without this set of questions, it comes out more natural, feels more like a podcast
turns.zh: 所以我求他们别开这个准备会，我觉得圆桌这样反而更好。不是说你不做准备，你可以自己准备，可以跟他们说说你想聊哪些内容。但没有那一套固定问题，聊出来会更自然，更像一档播客，

turns.en: than a boring conference panel. And can genuinely can ask follow-up questions for things I don't understand, things that interest me or I think would interest the audience. So anyway, conference rests. The conference had a bunch of talk about liquid alts and futures and ETFs. There was one on AI.
turns.zh: 而不是一场无聊的会议圆桌。而且我能真心实意地就自己不懂的、我感兴趣的、或我觉得观众会感兴趣的东西追问。总之，说说这场会。会上有一堆关于流动另类（liquid alts）、期货和 ETF 的讨论，还有一场讲 AI。

turns.en: General consensus there was it's not there yet. I disagree. One of my main takeaways was that discretionary macro is kind of the new emerging strategy du jour. These conferences used to be filled with plants, talking quant things, dazzling with stories about machine learning and models and customer risk logic, all the rest.
turns.zh: 普遍共识是 AI 还没到位（not there yet）。我不同意。我的主要收获之一是，主观宏观（discretionary macro）有点成了当下最热门的新兴策略（strategy du jour）。这类会议过去满台都是量化那套，用机器学习、模型、自定义风险逻辑之类的故事把你晃得眼花缭乱。

turns.en: But it just feels to me like all that is table stakes now, right? Like nobody's impressing you with how they use the computer, how they use data, how they use this even with AI. It's like, okay, everyone's doing that. So it used to separate you and make you different from the original discretionary futures
turns.zh: 但在我看来，这些如今都只是入场筹码（table stakes），对吧？没人会再因为你怎么用电脑、怎么用数据、甚至怎么用 AI 而对你刮目相看。就是'行吧，大家都在做'。所以过去这些能让你脱颖而出、把你和最早那批主观期货

turns.en: trader guys used to make you feel more safe. But now it feels like we've come full circle, right? And any manager has instant access to sophisticated programming and testing and trade tech and risk metrics and all the rest that don't raise any eyebrows anymore.
turns.zh: 交易员区分开、让人觉得更靠谱。但现在感觉我们绕了一整圈回来了，对吧？任何管理人现在都能随手用上复杂的编程、回测、交易技术、风险指标等等，这些再也不会让人惊讶了。

turns.en: And in fact, I think there's a bit of a feeling that anything anyone comes up with in a systematic way has already been done. There's already out there. You can get it at a bank risk premium desk. You can get it in a multi-strike. You can get it at any one of these places, I think, is some of this feeling.
turns.zh: 事实上，我觉得有那么一种感觉：任何人以系统化方式想出来的东西，早就有人做过了、市面上已经有了。你能在银行的风险溢价（risk premium）交易台拿到，能在多策略（multi-strat）机构拿到，能在这些地方随便哪一家拿到，我想这就是那种感觉的一部分。

turns.en: And that one of the only original trade generators left is the human brain, right? And so kind of this new bevy of discretionary guys who maybe think just like the old ones, but just different enough and fortunately in an unquantifiable way that they become
turns.zh: 也就是，剩下为数不多还能原创交易的'生成器'就是人脑了，对吧？于是有了一批新的主观交易人，他们的想法也许和老一辈一样，但又刚好有所不同，而且幸运地是以一种无法量化的方式不同，从而变得

turns.en: interesting portfolio pieces to people who've kind of done that been there with all the systematic pieces. So it was interesting to see a few of these guys around the conference and seems like I'm seeing more and more of this might just be anecdotal evidence, but it sure seems
turns.zh: 对那些系统化配置早就做过、玩过的人来说，是有意思的组合拼图。所以在会上看到几位这样的人挺有意思，而且我好像见到越来越多——这可能只是个人见闻（anecdotal evidence），但确实感觉

turns.en: like a zag from 10 years ago when it felt like there'd be no discretionary guys left and girls. And that would be all systematic. Maybe that is a preface for what happens to AI and the rest of the economy. All right. Number three, that Laker sale a few weeks ago, month and a half ago. So I'm a little late on this.
turns.zh: 这是跟 10 年前反着来（a zag）——那时候感觉以后不会再有主观交易员了，一切都会是系统化的。也许这正好是 AI 对经济其余部分冲击的一个前奏。好，第三罐：几周前、大概一个半月前那笔 Lakers（湖人队）出售，所以我聊得有点晚。

turns.en: I was trying to get a few guests to come on and talk about it. It's kind of interesting. A bunch of different pieces intersecting hedge funds, float, tax, all that. So I wanted to just spend a little time on it. We'll start with the seller, Mark Walter. This is all over the news.
turns.zh: 我本来想请几位嘉宾来聊聊，这事挺有意思，一堆不同的东西交织在一起——对冲基金、保险浮存金（float）、税务等等。所以我想花点时间讲讲。先从卖方 Mark Walter 说起，这事满新闻都是。

turns.en: You can Google it, go find out, but when I first heard it and people were getting mad that he was using insurance flow to purchase assets, investing the insurance premiums of little old ladies, I was getting mad because that's what Warren Buffett has been doing and trumpeting for decades, right? He's considered the king of this.
turns.zh: 你可以自己去 Google 查。但我第一次听说时，大家在气他用保险浮存金去买资产、拿老太太们的保费去投资，我却气的是另一回事——因为 Warren Buffett（巴菲特）几十年来一直在干这个、还一直高调宣扬，对吧？他被视为此中王者。

turns.en: So I'm like, wait, why is this anyone different? Everyone's selling options, getting premium to invest elsewhere. And that's the whole game, right? That's what insurance is used for from an investment side. I get it. I think they're buying sports teams with it and it seems, nothing's charged, nothing
turns.zh: 所以我就想，等等，这跟别人有啥不一样？大家都在卖期权、拿保费去别处投资，这就是整套玩法，对吧？从投资角度看，保险就是干这个用的。我懂。区别是他们拿这个去买体育球队，而且看起来——目前没人被起诉，什么

turns.en: is proven, but seems Mark Walter's went a little crazy with it. But they're all getting that he was basically loaning monies to affiliates, to buy all these teams or to pledge that capital to buy the teams, right? But the Dodgers, Dodgers TV, the Lakers, Chelsea, so anyway, all that is rather interesting
turns.zh: 都还没被证实——但 Mark Walter 这边似乎玩得有点过火。传出来的说法是，他基本上是把钱借给关联方去买这些球队，或者拿这些资本去质押买球队，对吧？涉及 Dodgers（道奇队）、Dodgers TV、Lakers、Chelsea（切尔西）。总之这些都挺有意思，

turns.en: and he was subpoenaed, all this stuff's coming out and he had to sell the Lakers. The flip side of that, the interesting side, now the buyer, right? Sure, there was a poor seller, but conveniently SpaceX stock gets unlocked August 6th and the new buyer comes in and purchased this August 12th.
turns.zh: 他收到了传票（subpoena），这些东西都曝了出来，他不得不卖掉 Lakers。另一面、也就是有意思的一面，是买方。当然，有个倒霉的卖方，但巧的是 SpaceX 的股票在 8 月 6 日解禁，新买家 8 月 12 日就进场买下了。

turns.en: So that was Iger and Kushner's brother, but did you know under the tax law they can amortize the current value of those player contracts over the next 15 years? So I had Claude do some math on that and showed me, take it for what it's worth, but showed me that that's about $800 million a year in deductions.
turns.zh: 买家是 Iger 和 Kushner 的兄弟。但你知道吗，根据税法，他们可以在未来 15 年里对这些球员合同的现值进行摊销（amortize）。我让 Claude（AI 助手）算了笔账——姑且一听——它告诉我这大约相当于每年 8 亿美元（$800 million）的税前扣除。

turns.en: So for two guys sitting there, right, and they're big in the, I don't have the name of their firm in front of me, but ventures slash private equity that got into SpaceX, got into open AI, another company that SpaceX purchased. So two guys sitting on a few billion dollars and unrealized gains that they could perhaps
turns.zh: 所以这两位，他们在——我手头没有他们公司的名字——风险投资／私募股权（ventures / private equity）领域做得很大，投进了 SpaceX，投进了 OpenAI，还有另一家被 SpaceX 收购的公司。两个人手握几十亿美元（a few billion）的未实现收益（unrealized gains），也许很快就能

turns.en: be unlocking soon, open AI has delayed their IPO, but for sure one day happened. So it's going to save them a ton of tax, right? They get that $800 million deduction, they've got all that SpaceX AI money coming in. So and then they get to own the Lakers after the fact.
turns.zh: 解锁变现——OpenAI 推迟了 IPO，但总有一天会上市。所以这会帮他们省下一大笔税，对吧？他们拿到那 8 亿美元的扣除，又有那么多 SpaceX、AI 的钱进账，然后事后还白得一支 Lakers。

turns.en: Steve Bommer, who's himself in trouble for scurrying some of the roles did all this when he bought the Clippers, again, some cloud research there shows about 600 million or so of losses on those tax returns, despite the value of the franchise going up.
turns.zh: Steve Ballmer（鲍尔默）本人也因为一些税务／角色问题惹上麻烦，他当年买 Clippers（快船队）时也玩了同一套。同样是我用 Claude 做的研究显示，那些报税表上大约有 6 亿美元（600 million）左右的亏损，尽管球队本身的价值在上涨。

turns.en: So cool story to me, they weren't just buying a scarce trophy asset, they're buying a deduction and tax savings also. And right, what's that worth to someone with that money gains and then also makes me think just right, if half the brain power and money and time spent all the time on saving money
